questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academics and the opportunity to meet people from everywhere around the world

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Meeting people from everywhere around the world and not having to think about anything other than studying was a great experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, but you had to put in a lot of work

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot - I had to figure out most things myself. There were a lot of mails and information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The Golden Bear Orientation was catered for American students who have never touched alcohol, partied, lived by themselves etc. Very irrelevant for Danish students who are generally older and much more independent

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Coops, I-House

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans in I-House, you could also cook for yourself

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Go live in I-House

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I-House was an amazing experience, one of the best of my life. However, it was really expensive, so it gets a 4

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a lot of work to figure out whether you were eligible for different courses. On the day of the registration, the webpage went down, meaning that all UCPH students could not register for the courses. The courses got filled up, and we were left with the leftovers

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was an initial drag-and-drop period where the students try out different courses. It was hectic in the first weeks as you were trying to follow many courses without knowing if you were gonna get them, as you most liekly were waitlisted. Also, you could only waitlist in one course as an exchange student

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2/3 in the end. They were not very competitive tho

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I heard that the CS courses were really good; i wish i tried some of them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was OK; engaging professors and very research focused. The academic level was lower than in UCPH, but workload higher

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could only take undergrad courses; the level was definitely lower than in Denmark, but the workload was big during the semester

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different; a lot of work and assignments during the semester and the grades were grades through the semester. The relation to the professors and instructors were much more personal

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ECON172, ECON191, ECON131, POLSCI179

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ECON172, Development Economics, with Ted Miguel was really engaging and he is an academic superstar. You also really get to know applied econometrics and specifically IV, RD, RCT and DD methods, which we don't really use so much in UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't expect to travel so much during the semester, but I am so glad I did

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is very expensive in the Bay Area

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You could swim, play tennis, basket and everything.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cal day, game days etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to a lot of campus activities, see the basket, gymnastics, football games. Go travel a lot!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the national parks, especially Yosemite

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was OK; however, there were some culture shocks that were bigger than expected. Homelessness and inequality especially. In short: Denmark is good and USA is pretty shit

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to everyone and be more open than you usually would be

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Homelessness, general feeling of unsafety unlike in Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Innovative spirit at Berkeley, Americans are very open and easy to talk to, it was inspiring to be surrounded by a lot of smart people that really believes in themselves.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to I-House, make a lot of friends and talk to everyone, go on trips which will really cement your friendship, put academics second while you're on exchange as you'll gain so much more and you can always tryhard in UCPH

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I-House, making friends from everywhere around the world and travelling

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to Berkeley as there were so many practicalities that took so long time. It was immense

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to I-House

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
